article_title: Short-duration podcasts as a supplementary learning tool: perceptions of medical students and impact on assessment performance.
citation: Prakash S.S., Muthuraman N., Anand R. (2017). Short-duration podcasts as a supplementary learning tool: perceptions of medical students and impact on assessment performance. BMC Medical Education 17:167. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-017-1001-5
title: 3-MinuTe Lessons (3MTLs): eight audiovisual podcasts of ≤3 minutes as lecture supplements
description: 3MTLs were eight short (≤3 min) audiovisual podcasts covering two biochemistry topics, each consisting of "a graphical slide show with a video inset of the narrator in each slide", produced with PowerPoint and Office Mix at 320 × 240 resolution with file sizes between 6.2 to 8.8 MB, targeted at small-screen devices. They were released on the institution's e-learning portal after each didactic lecture, and each episode listed specific learning objectives (Table 1).
requirements: Released after the corresponding didactic lecture so students can use them for review
Pre-written script tailored to fit the time-frame, rehearsed before recording
constraints: Limited information can be conveyed due to the time barrier
Production of each episode required around 6–8 h
Download/streaming on the e-learning portal was the lowest-rated quality aspect
target_learning_goals: Biochemistry content review: fat-soluble vitamins, heme metabolism and hemoglobin disorders
examples: Table 1 lists the eight episodes with durations (e.g., Vitamin A, 3′ 00ʼ; Porphyrias, 2′ 59ʼ) and total views ranging from 44 to 91
